Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Draft MAP and an abbreviated evaluation plan attached (lumen-turnstart-map-20260829.xlsx). Summary below.

Summary of proposed MAP & eval scope:
- Objective: Validate turn-start (first-token) latency and streaming token latencies for our chat model variant under realistic LumenAI prompt mix.
- Metrics to report:
  - Turn-start TTFT (time from request receipt to first token emitted) at p50/p95/p99
  - Streaming per-token latency distribution (p50/p95/p99 for tokens after first token)
  - End-to-end response tail (complete response generation) for longer-turn prompts (p95/p99)
  - Throughput/concurrency: sustained QPS targets and max sustainable concurrency with <200ms increase in p95 TTFT
- Workloads: 3 canonical prompt buckets (short-turn, mid-turn, long-turn) based on LumenAI sample prompts you shared. We'll instrument with 10k requests per bucket over multiple runs.
- Concurrency envelope: 1, 8, 32, 128 concurrent sessions (session = single streaming connection; each session may issue sequential turns).
- Environment: Redwood Hosted (us-west), model: open-llama-chat-v2-ggml-quantized (config attached), 8-GPU reserved node group equivalent to proposed Dedicated tier.
- Artifacts we will deliver: CSV of per-request timestamps (request_received, request_dispatched, first_token_emitted, last_token_emitted), aggregated p50/p95/p99 tables, raw traces, and the MAP workbook.

Preliminary numbers from our internal run (single 2-hour run; synthetic Lumen prompt mix):
- Turn-start (TTFT) p50 = 42 ms, p95 = 110 ms, p99 = 220 ms (at concurrency=8)
- Streaming per-token p95 = 15 ms (median token generation ~9 ms), p99 tokens see jumps up to 120 ms under GC/IO spikes on older kernels
- Throughput: sustained 720 tokens/s per GPU at quantized config; observed graceful degradation up to concurrency=64, with p95 TTFT increase +170 ms at concurrency=64 in this config.

Next steps proposed:
1) Run the MAP with your actual prompt sample set Wednesday (Aug 31) — would you be able to provide a 2k-sample prompt export by EOD Monday?
2) We'll run three 1-hour sweeps across the concurrency envelope and deliver the CSVs and an executive summary within 24 hours of completion.

Please see the attached workbook for the canonical test harness, API call traces, and the template for acceptance criteria.

Thanks,

Emma/Priya — quick technical notes to set expectations for the MAP run: 

- Turn-start (TTFT) definition: we'll measure as the delta between server request_received timestamp (ingress) and the first byte of the streaming chunk sent to client. Our CSV export will include timestamps with microsecond precision; we will also provide gRPC-level trace IDs for cross-correlation.
- Noise sources: when we see p99 spikes they typically correlate with either kernel preemption during batch formation or network TX queueing in the NAT gateway. For the MAP run we recommend: 1) short maintenance window (no infra changes), 2) pin a single model binary variant (no autoscaling), and 3) run three replicate sweeps to compute robust tails.
- Concurrency sizing: the 128 concurrent sessions target is mostly to measure tail behavior — we expect p95 deterioration but want to confirm graceful fallback behavior (model variant routing). If Lumen wants a hard SLA at concurrency=128 we will need a dedicated node group sizing proposal (I can draft).
- Deliverables: raw CSVs (attached), aggregated CSV with p50/p95/p99 columns, and a small script to reproduce the rollups using the timestamps.

I'll be on the run Wednesday but can join the test kickoff call if needed.

—Rishi
